basis: docs/preliminary-design.md: 'Detailed seat geometry, loads, tolerances, retention, actuator dynamics and physical performance require their own commissioned evidence.' These gates hold that evidence. Each gate names its owner phase and the result that reopens preliminary design.

gates.test: Bench rig: two floor belts, two pinch lanes and the hood at R3 positions; 24 FUEL loaded as a heap
gates.pass: At least 22 pinch-sensor crossings within 12 s, with at most one jam, in each of 5 trials
gates.adverse: 30 FUEL with the rig tilted 10 degrees toward a side plate: no jam needs a reversal longer than 0.5 s
gates.byCalculation: At belt speed, two lanes at 0.6 m/s and 154 mm spacing would feed 7.8 FUEL/s. The launch trial's single free FUEL rolls on that belt at 0.22 m/s from rest, which is 1.4 FUEL/s per lane and 2.8 for two lanes against 2.00, so the rate depends on how a stacked batch rides the belt. The launch trial's wheel does 28 J of work per FUEL, which two flywheel motors replace between shots; the speed drop inside one shot is gate G5
gates.onFail: Rotating indexer or a third lane; reopen the whole-robot comparison if that also fails

gates.test: Robot loaded with 24 FUEL, ten stops from 3 m/s at 0.5 g and five 0.5 g turns
gates.pass: At most one FUEL leaves the robot across all runs
gates.byCalculation: Front lip 61 mm above the floor belts: by statics a floor FUEL needs about 5.2 g of horizontal deceleration to roll over it; side and rear walls rise above the top layer. The seated FUEL has no forward restraint (gate G7)
gates.onFail: Passive one-way flap across the intake throat

gates.test: Robot at 70.3 kg seated at 0, +25 and -25 mm lateral offset; lift 70 mm; remove power for 3 s
gates.pass: Hook slip under 5 mm, at least 5 mm clearance to carpet and TOWER BASE throughout, brake holds 1.5 x 690 N
gates.byCalculation: hang_overlap.py (plan view): both uprights bear for lateral offsets up to +/-23.9 mm with the 714 mm frame (+/-6.9 mm at 680 mm); 0.5 deg yaw leaves a 7.5 mm trailing gap, so the robot squares against both uprights before lifting. The side-view hang trial at 70.3 kg holds 37.5 mm with the brake and fails without it. The cable load peaks at 1043 N during the lift and settles at 690 N.
gates.onFail: Spring latch under the rung or wider frame within the 2794 mm perimeter

gates.test: Bench intake at 17.5, 20 and 25 mm compression, belt driven by the selected motor
gates.pass: 20 of 20 floor FUEL captured within 1.0 s; loaded belt speed stays at or above 2.5 m/s
gates.byCalculation: Acquisition physics trials pass at 17.5 mm and 2.5 m/s and fail at 15 mm and 2.0 m/s; bumper friction 0.3 passes and 0.2 fails; peak contact power 786 W at the imposed 3 m/s, above the intake's 30 A supply limit
gates.onFail: Reselect the belt motor or gearing; revise the pinch

gates.objective: Shot calibration at the 2.7 m pose
gates.test: Measure exit speed and spin off the hood and the wheel speed through each shot; shoot 20 FUEL from the 2.7 m pose
gates.pass: Measured release inside 6.70-7.00 m/s at the 6.86 m/s setpoint through every shot of a 24 FUEL batch, and at least 19 of 20 scored
gates.byCalculation: The launch trial releases at 6.86 m/s and 61.9 degrees from a 13.4 m/s wheel surface. Delivery trials from that release state score from 6.70 to 7.00 m/s (plus or minus 2.2%) at the nominal drag and spin lift and at all four corners; 6.55 m/s misses at the high-drag, high-spin corner and 7.15 m/s at both low-drag corners. Launch trials pass at 13.1 and 13.6 m/s wheel surface and fail at 13.0 and 13.8 m/s. The trial holds the wheel speed; its 28 J of wheel work per FUEL is a 6.8% speed drop for a free 0.006 kg m2 wheel, three times the band
gates.onFail: Speed feedforward and more flywheel current; adjust the hood end angle. More inertia does not fit the weight reserve: 2% droop needs about 0.020 kg m2, at least 7.7 kg at the rim, against 1.76 kg

gates.test: Cross the BUMP ten times in each direction with the intake retracted
gates.pass: No high-centering and no robot part other than wheels and bumpers touches the BUMP
gates.byCalculation: bump_crossing.py: 8.7 mm least clearance (front bumper corner), 24 mm at the belly over a sharp crest
gates.onFail: Select R3L and the TRENCH route

gates.objective: Stage the first FUEL and launch it with the flywheel at speed
gates.test: Bench lane with the floor belts, flywheel and hood at R3 positions: one FUEL thrown in at the intake's capture velocity with the belts stopped; then back-off, spin-up and feed. Repeat with the FUEL pressed 3 mm into the stopped wheel, and after a 0.5 g stop in each direction
gates.pass: With the back-off in the sequence: 10 of 10 FUEL at rest on the belt no more than 1 mm into the stopped wheel, and 10 of 10 released inside 6.70-7.00 m/s with the wheel at speed; wheel-to-hood squeeze between 8 and 16 mm
gates.adverse: Floor belt left running during entry: the FUEL must not be fed before the wheel reaches speed
gates.byCalculation: Entry trial: at rest against the stopped wheel, 0.02 mm into it, belts stopped; at lower contact damping it rests 7 to 62 mm clear. A belt running at 0.05 m/s or more presses it 3.2 to 5.9 mm in (fail). Launch trials: back-off, spin-up and feed release at 6.86 m/s. Without the back-off a FUEL at rest 0.02 or 0.23 mm into the stopped wheel still scores; at 0.44 mm or 3.2 mm in, the wheel takes it during spin-up and releases near 1.5 m/s (the 0.23/0.44 mm threshold is a penalty-contact property, not a measurement). With the back-off the 3.2 mm seat scores. A FUEL wedged 5.9 mm in is not freed by the back-off. Squeeze 8 and 16 mm pass, 6 and 20 mm fail; wheel friction 0.5 passes, 0.3 fails; contact stiffness 10 and 30 kN/m pass, 7.5 kN/m fails
gates.onFail: Add a hold-back (a gate or feeder ahead of the flywheel); that moves the pinch forward and reopens the hopper layout
